title: Drift-aware integration & regression harness for INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ) quant profiles
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Build and validate an integration and nightly regression harness that runs INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (both GPTQ and AWQ variants) end-to-end against a representative model matrix, with drift-aware calibration checks and automated canary gating.

Background: We have multiple pipelines for weight-only INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ) profiles, but coverage across model families, sequence-length distributions, and hardware variants is fragmented. Recent customer reports show intermittent quality regressions that only appear after long-running traffic shifts. This ticket centralizes an integration path + regression suite to catch accuracy drift and calibration mismatches before deploy.

Goals:
- Validate that GPTQ and AWQ profiles integrated into the profile registry do not produce > regression thresholds on a curated prompt set across models (Llama2-family, Mistral-family, and 7B/13B variants).
- Add drift detection: nightly comparison of calibration statistics (scale/zero-point distributions, activation histograms) and automatic creation of investigation alerts when change exceeds thresholds.
- End-to-end canary flow: run a canary deployment that performs shadow quantized inference, compare outputs with baseline FP16 and existing INT8 golden seeds, and auto-fail rollout when unacceptable drift is observed.

Scope:
- Integrate quantization profile artifacts (GPTQ/AWQ) into the CI runner for integration tests.
- Implement a regression job in the orchestration layer that: pulls models from the profile registry, runs calibration sweep, executes eval prompt suite, and posts structured telemetry.
- Implement lightweight drift detector comparing nightly metrics vs last successful baseline.
- Wire alerting to internal Slack channel and an internal dashboard.

Non-goals:
- Full performance micro-optimizations of kernels (separate runtime optimization tickets).
- Long-term retention of telemetry beyond 90 days (handled by observability team).

Success metrics:
- Nightly job runs for 90% of target model matrix without infra failures.
- No false negatives: regression jobs should surface known historical regressions in synthetic replay tests 100% of the time.
- Canary gating prevents at least one rollout with regression > degradation threshold during rollout window (measured during pilot).
acceptance_criteria: Nightly regression job runs and completes for the primary model matrix (Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B, Redwood-7B) within the SUT window and reports pass/fail status.
Drift detector emits an alert when calibration metric (per-layer scale variance) increases by > 15% vs baseline and creates a ticket in the quantization backlog automatically.
Canary flow rejects a simulated regression case (injected degradation) and triggers rollback/fallback according to rollout policy documented in console-2025.02.
Integration tests include structured telemetry that mirrors production tokens/sequence length distributions and are visible in the cost/latency dashboard for cross-team review.
Runbook added to Confluence describing how to triage failed regressions, rebaseline, and request a rollback; reviewed and approved by PM and Observability owners.
tasks: (2d) Create integration runner job that accepts profile artifact URIs and model keys; smoke test with a single Mistral-7B profile.
(3d) Implement nightly regression workflow in orchestration layer: calibration -> eval suite -> structured telemetry export.
(1d) Add drift detection logic and thresholds; write unit tests for detector using synthetic variance inputs.
(2d) Build canary shadow pipeline that runs quantized model in parallel with FP16 baseline and computes side-by-side metrics; wire into rollout policy.
(1d) Add dashboard panels (telemetry team collaboration) and Slack alert hook; provide example alerts for monitor owners.
(1d) Draft Confluence runbook and include troubleshooting checklist and rebaseline instructions.
(1d) Coordinate with Reliability to schedule first canary pilot and capture results; create follow-ups if infra flakiness observed.
